quick_notes.title: Classical Dances (8)
quick_notes.detail: Bharatnatyam (TN), Kathak (UP), Kathakali (Kerala), Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (AP), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), Sattriya (Assam).
quick_notes.explanation: India officially recognizes eight classical dance forms, each originating from a specific region and following strict rules from an ancient text called the Natya Shastra. The eight dances are: Bharatanatyam from Tamil Nadu, Kathak from Uttar Pradesh, Kathakali from Kerala, Mohiniyattam from Kerala, Kuchipudi from Andhra Pradesh, Odissi from Odisha, Manipuri from Manipur, and Sattriya from Assam. Bharatanatyam is known for its fixed upper body and rhythmic footwork, while Kathak focuses on fast spins and storytelling through footwork. Kathakali uses elaborate makeup and dramatic eye movements to tell stories from Hindu epics, and Mohiniyattam is a graceful, feminine dance performed by women. Kuchipudi combines dance with dialogue, Odissi features a characteristic hip sway and curved posture, and Manipuri is gentle and flowing, often depicting the love story of Radha and Krishna. Sattriya, the newest addition, was traditionally performed in monasteries of Assam and is based on devotional themes.

quick_notes.title: Folk Dances (Set 1)
quick_notes.detail: Bihu (Assam), Garba (Gujarat), Lavani (Maharashtra), Ghoomar (Rajasthan), Nautanki (UP), Yakshagana (Karnataka).
quick_notes.explanation: Folk dances are traditional dances that belong to a specific region or community and are performed during festivals or celebrations. Bihu is a lively dance from Assam, performed during the harvest festival of the same name. Garba is a circular dance from Gujarat, often done during the Navratri festival to honor the goddess Durga. Lavani is a powerful dance from Maharashtra, known for its fast beats and sung by female performers. Ghoomar is a graceful dance from Rajasthan, where women spin in circles wearing long, flowing skirts. Nautanki is a folk theatre style from Uttar Pradesh that combines dance, music, and storytelling, while Yakshagana is a traditional dance-drama from Karnataka that tells stories from Hindu epics with elaborate costumes and makeup.

quick_notes.title: Folk Dances (Set 2)
quick_notes.detail: Raut Nacha (Chhattisgarh), Cheraw (Mizoram - Bamboo dance), Chhau (WB/Jharkhand/Odisha), Karagam (TN).
quick_notes.explanation: Raut Nacha is a folk dance from Chhattisgarh performed by the Yadav community to celebrate the festival of Diwali. Cheraw, also called the Bamboo dance, comes from Mizoram and involves dancers stepping in and out of moving bamboo poles. Chhau is a traditional dance from West Bengal, Jharkhand, and Odisha that tells stories from Hindu mythology using masks and vigorous movements. Karagam is a folk dance from Tamil Nadu where performers balance decorated pots on their heads while dancing to rhythmic music.

quick_notes.title: Major Festivals
quick_notes.detail: Onam (Kerala - Boat race), Pongal (TN), Hornbill (Nagaland), Losar (Ladakh/Sikkim), Chapchar Kut (Mizoram).
quick_notes.explanation: Onam is a harvest festival celebrated in the state of Kerala, and its main event is a boat race called the Vallam Kali. Pongal is a four-day harvest festival from the state of Tamil Nadu, where people cook a special dish of rice and milk in a new pot to thank the sun god. Hornbill is a festival named after the hornbill bird, held in the state of Nagaland to showcase the traditional dances and songs of the Naga tribes. Losar is the Tibetan New Year festival, celebrated in the regions of Ladakh and the state of Sikkim, with prayers and family feasts. Chapchar Kut is a spring festival from the state of Mizoram, where people celebrate the end of the bamboo-cutting season by wearing colorful clothes and performing traditional dances.

quick_notes.title: Musical Instruments
quick_notes.detail: Sitar (Ravi Shankar), Sarod (Amjad Ali Khan), Flute (Hariprasad Chaurasia), Tabla (Zakir Hussain).
quick_notes.explanation: The sitar is a plucked string instrument used in Hindustani classical music, and Ravi Shankar was a famous sitar player who introduced it to the world. The sarod is another plucked string instrument that produces a deeper, more resonant sound than the sitar, and Amjad Ali Khan is a celebrated sarod maestro. The flute, specifically the bamboo bansuri, is a wind instrument blown across a hole, and Hariprasad Chaurasia is a master of the Hindustani flute. The tabla is a pair of hand drums, one wooden and one metal, used to create rhythms, and Zakir Hussain is a legendary tabla player. These four musicians are among the most respected performers of Indian classical music.
